_comment_why_json: JSON and not YAML because scripts/lab_alarm.py runs under launchd on the brew interpreter with no virtual environment (Operating Rule 11). A YAML config would put a third-party import on the path of a timer whose entire value is that it keeps running unattended. OMN-18867.
_comment_why_env_refs: ${ONEX_INFRA_HOST} and ${ONEX_RUNTIME_SSH_HOST} are expanded at load and RAISE when unset. A literal lab address here would be the hardcoded-host defect Operating Rule 6 forbids, and a silent empty default would be the Rule 8 one.
_comment_docker_transport: docker_command still reaches container_restarts through ssh at the runner seam (the lab lane runs on the lab box, not on the host this timer runs on, and a local docker daemon cannot see the lane's containers at all). OMN-19091: consumer_group_lag no longer uses this transport at all -- it reads the broker in-process via aiokafka, using the ~/.onex dev-lane identity, because rpk has no credential-input mechanism that keeps a value off argv (ruling of 2026-09-21).
_comment_kafka_bootstrap: The dev lane's external SASL_PLAINTEXT listener, dialed directly from this Mac -- the same address hook_edge_lane.yaml declares for the dev lane's workstation clients. No docker_command rewrite: this connection never goes through ssh.
_comment_sha_surfaces: The delivered sha is resolved from the deploy agent first and the runtime /ready second. Measured 2026-09-21: this lane's /ready answers healthy and carries a package version with no commit anywhere in its payload, while the agent answered with a 40-hex sha on the same host at the same moment. A resolver on /ready alone would report unresolved on a healthy lane forever.
_comment_restart_bounds: Per container, not one fleet number. A broker that has never restarted and a runtime recreated on every deploy do not share a threshold, and one number for both is either noise or blindness. omnimarket-projection-savings-writer carries the tightest bound because it is the container that crash-looped unobserved for nine days (OMN-18851).
_comment_groups: The standalone projection-writer groups declared by docker/docker-compose.dev-lane.yml KAFKA_CONSUMER_GROUP values, the same derivation scripts/runtime_build/declared_consumer_groups.py performs for the lab-pass receipt. savings-writer is the group that sat at lag 498 for nine days.
_comment_effects_group: OMN-19091: the delegate-skill runtime-effects consumer group embeds the node's own contract_version (measured drifting 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0 mid-session), so it is matched by this stable prefix/suffix rather than one pinned literal -- scripts/runtime_build/declared_consumer_groups.py names exactly this staleness failure mode. Five occurrences on 2026-09-21 (18:47:53, 19:55:09, 20:27:38, 20:57:50, 21:29:04Z, roughly six minutes each) were each found only by a lane tripping over a delegation refusal, never by a monitor.
_comment_runtime_ancestor: OMN-18867 (2026-09-28): the deploy agent rebuilds at origin/dev, so the delivered sha is routinely a merge the rebuild trigger calls non-runtime, which never gets a receipt of its own. The receipt is asked of the nearest runtime-affecting first-parent ancestor, by the staging gate's own rule and omniclaude's deploy-gate path validator. Asking the exact sha read INDETERMINATE 03:25Z-11:25Z on 2026-09-28 while the ancestors carried PASS.
_comment_work_ledger_db_container: OMN-20248: work_ledger_db_container is the dev lane's postgres container the work_ledger_projection_stale condition reads max(row_ts) of omninode_internal.work_ledger_rows from, through docker_command (docker exec ... psql, read-only).
_comment_work_ledger_database: OMN-20248: work_ledger_database is the database holding omninode_internal.work_ledger_rows. Measured 2026-10-01: that table sat frozen at 424 rows for about 36 hours while the projection's consumer groups read Stable at lag 0, so only a file-vs-table comparison sees the freeze.
_comment_work_ledger_max_lag_minutes: OMN-20248: work_ledger_max_lag_minutes is how far the projection's max(row_ts) may trail the newest canonical row in the --ledger file before the condition alarms. Thirty minutes is well past normal emit-to-projection latency and well inside the hourly tick, so one tick sees a freeze.
_comment_chain_canary: OMN-20594: the delegation_chain_canary condition reads the verdict of chain_canary_workflow (chain-canary.yml, C15) on chain_canary_branch through the workflow-verdict reader staging delivery binds C15 with, scheduled runs only. It alarms when the newest completed scheduled run is not success or started more than chain_canary_max_age_minutes ago. 180 minutes is one 2-hour C15 period plus slack, the same 3-hour bound deliver-dev-candidate-to-staging.yml reads C15 with. The h201 dev lane this canary grades is the protected delegation lane (deploy/lane-census/lane-manifest.yaml).
_comment_census_command: OMN-19418: census_command reads the live snapshot the existing lane-census timer writes on the lab host and emits on its census bus topics. It never reads the checked-in snapshot. A lane-census.json in the alarm state directory is the fixture injection seam. census_max_age_minutes is two hours: one hourly census period plus slack; missing, invalid or stale data stays INDETERMINATE and feeds the existing stale alarm.
